c.tagline: Hanseatic port of fairy-tale musicians, a UNESCO market square, and the winding Schnoor.

taxi.fareNote: Fares are metered and regulated; you can hail on the street, wait at a rank, or book by phone or app. Ride-hailing apps FreeNow, Uber and Bolt also operate.

emergency.note: 112 is the EU-wide emergency number for ambulance and fire; 110 reaches the police. Both are free and staffed by English-speaking operators.

english.label: Easy to get by in English

hood_landmark.Altstadt: Bremen Marktplatz Town Hall and Roland

avoid.reason: Caution around the Hauptbahnhof and the Viertel at night

hood_desc: Bremen's historic core on the north bank of the Weser, built around the Marktplatz with the UNESCO-listed Gothic-and-Renaissance Town Hall (Rathaus) and the Roland statue, the bronze Town Musicians of Bremen, the Dom St. Petri and the expressionist brick lane of Böttcherstrasse; best for first-timers who want the landmarks, shopping and restaurants on foot.

Bremen's oldest quarter, a maze of tiny 15th-to-18th-century fishermen's and craftsmen's cottages now filled with galleries, jewellers, cafes and restaurants; the most picturesque and romantic place to stay, though small and busy by day.

The bohemian heart of Bremen along Ostertorsteinweg and Vor dem Steintor, packed with indie bars, restaurants, theatres, vintage shops, street art and the Kunsthalle art museum; best for nightlife, dining and a young, alternative crowd.

An affluent, leafy residential district of Gruenderzeit and Art Nouveau villas east of the centre, bordering the huge Buergerpark; quiet, green and elegant, good for travellers wanting calm and parks a short tram ride from the sights.

A regenerated harbour district on the Weser west of the centre, where former docks and warehouses now hold loft apartments, waterfront restaurants, event spaces and design hotels; a modern, spacious area for those who like riverside industrial-chic over old-town bustle.

water.note: Tap water is strictly regulated and safe to drink.

transit.hours: Trams and buses run roughly 4:30am to around 1am; a Nachteule night-bus and night-tram network covers Friday and Saturday nights.
transit.pay: No tap-in gates: buy tickets in the FahrPlaner/BSAG app, at machines, or from the driver, and have them ready before boarding; one ticket covers BSAG trams and buses across the VBN network. A single ride is about €3.05 (~$3.30) and a day ticket about €8.60. Staying weeks? The €58/month Deutschland-Ticket covers local transit nationwide.

bus: ZOB Bremen (Central Bus Station, beside Hauptbahnhof)
ferry: Martinianleger (Weser river ferries and excursion boats)

transit.m: Tram line 6 to Hauptbahnhof / city centre (~11-15 min, every 10 min)

tip.r: Service is included by law; locals round the bill up to the next euro or add about 5-10% for good service, handed to the server rather than left on the table.

food.name: Knipp
food.desc: Bremen's coarse sausage of pork, oats and offal, fried in slices until crisp and served with fried potatoes, pickled gherkins and apple sauce.

places.name: Gaststaette Kleiner Olymp
places.note: Tiny historic tavern in the Schnoor lanes and the standard address for Bremen home cooking.

places.name: Bremer Ratskeller

places.name: Schroeter's Leib und Seele
places.note: Neighbourhood restaurant in the old quarter with regional Bremen dishes on a changing menu.

food.name: Kohl und Pinkel
food.desc: Winter kale stewed with oats and lard, served with the smoked Pinkel sausage, kassler and boiled potatoes - the north's cold-weather feast.

places.name: Gaststaette Kleiner Olymp
places.note: One of the reliable places to eat kale and Pinkel in the traditional style, in season.

places.name: Schuettinger Gasthausbrauerei
places.note: House brewpub beside the market square, hearty north German plates with its own beer.

food.name: Labskaus
food.desc: Sailor's mash of corned beef, potato and beetroot, crowned with a fried egg, rollmops and gherkins - looks alarming, tastes salty and comforting.

places.name: Bremer Ratskeller
places.note: Classic version served under the town hall vaults; a Bremen rite of passage.

places.name: Gaststaette Kleiner Olymp
places.note: Traditional pub kitchen doing labskaus with all the correct garnishes.

places.name: Schlachte promenade restaurants
places.note: Riverfront row of north German taverns and ship-themed bars serving sailor food.

food.name: Bremer Kuekenragout
food.desc: The city's grand old dish - poached chicken in a creamy white sauce with asparagus, peas, crayfish and veal quenelles, served in a pastry shell.

places.name: Bremer Ratskeller
places.note: Keeps the historic Bremen recipes on the menu when few other kitchens still do.

places.name: Gaststaette Kleiner Olymp
places.note: Traditional Bremen menu that includes the old bourgeois ragout dishes.

places.name: Schroeter's Leib und Seele
places.note: Regional cooking with seasonal asparagus specialities in spring.

food.name: Nordsee crab and matjes
food.desc: Hand-peeled North Sea brown shrimp piled on buttered brown bread, or young salted matjes herring with onion, cream and new potatoes.

places.name: Schlachte promenade restaurants
places.note: Weser-side terraces where the fish and shrimp dishes come with a river view.

places.name: Bremer Ratskeller
places.note: North Sea fish starters and matjes in season, with the country's oldest wine cellar attached.

places.name: Domshof Wochenmarkt
places.note: Weekday market with fish counters selling crab rolls and matjes to eat standing up.

food.name: Bremer Klaben
food.desc: Dense Bremen fruit loaf packed with raisins, candied peel and almonds, baked from November and eaten in thin buttered slices all winter.

places.name: Konditorei Knigge
places.note: Bremen's best known confectioner, baking Klaben and Bremer Kluten sweets for generations.

places.name: Domshof Wochenmarkt
places.note: Market bakers sell Klaben by the slab in the run-up to Christmas.

places.name: Bremer Weihnachtsmarkt
places.note: Christmas market stalls around the town hall stock Klaben alongside the Schlachte medieval market.

food.name: Beck's and Haake-Beck
food.desc: Beck's has been brewed on the Weser since 1873; the local Haake-Beck Kraeusen, cloudy and unfiltered, is what Bremen residents actually drink.

places.name: Schuettinger Gasthausbrauerei
places.note: Bremen's oldest house brewery, pouring its own unfiltered beer beside the market square.

places.name: Schlachte promenade beer gardens
places.note: Long riverside strip of terraces and beer gardens, the city's default summer drinking spot.

places.name: Beck's in'n Snoor
places.note: Small traditional pub in the old lanes for a Beck's or a Kraeusen without the crowds.

food.name: German wine at the Ratskeller
food.desc: The Bremer Ratskeller holds the oldest cask of German wine in the world and pours only German bottles - Riesling and Mosel by the glass in the vaults.

places.name: Bremer Ratskeller
places.note: Six centuries of German wine under the town hall; guided cellar tours end in a tasting.

places.name: Schroeter's Leib und Seele
places.note: Small, well chosen German wine list to go with the regional menu.

places.name: Katzen-Cafe
places.note: Long-running Schnoor restaurant with a courtyard terrace and a broad wine selection.

landmarks: Bremen Town Hall (Rathaus)
A UNESCO-listed Gothic hall dressed in a flamboyant Weser Renaissance facade, its Ratskeller below stores Germany's oldest working wine barrels.
Roland Statue
This 1404 stone knight on the Marktplatz, a UNESCO symbol of civic liberty, has guarded Bremen's independence for over six centuries.
Bremen Town Musicians Statue
Gerhard Marcks' bronze donkey, dog, cat and rooster immortalize the Grimm fairy tale; grasping the donkey's polished front legs is said to grant wishes.
Schnoor Quarter
Bremen's oldest district is a dollhouse maze of fifteenth-century fishermen's cottages, now filled with artisan workshops, cafes and a year-round Christmas shop.
Böttcherstraße
A 100-meter expressionist fantasy street of brick, built by coffee magnate Ludwig Roselius in the 1920s, crowned by the golden Lichtbringer relief and Paula Modersohn-Becker Museum.
St Peter's Cathedral (Bremer Dom)
Twin 98-meter spires mark this 1,200-year-old cathedral, whose lead cellar famously displays mummified corpses and whose tower climb surveys the Marktplatz.
Marktplatz
One of Europe's loveliest market squares assembles town hall, cathedral, Roland and gabled guild houses like the ornate Schütting into a single ensemble.
Schlachte Embankment
Bremen's medieval river harbor is now a lively Weser promenade of beer gardens, historic ships and summer terraces facing the sunset.
Universum Bremen
A gleaming silver science center shaped like a whale-clam hybrid invites hands-on exploration of technology, the human body and planet Earth.
Bürgerpark
A vast nineteenth-century landscaped park of lakes, meadows and animal enclosures, financed entirely by citizens and still Bremen's beloved green retreat.

train.note: Bremen Hauptbahnhof is a handsome brick terminus about ten minutes' walk north of the Altstadt and the Marktplatz. It sits on the ICE corridor from Hamburg through to the Ruhr and Cologne, so Hamburg is about an hour, Hanover an hour, Cologne 3h and Munich around 6h30. No train crosses a border from Bremen: for Amsterdam change at Osnabruck or Hanover onto the ICE International via Bad Bentheim, and for Copenhagen change at Hamburg. Regional trains and the Bremen S-Bahn network cover Bremerhaven, Oldenburg, Delmenhorst and Bremervorde.

bus.note: Long-distance coaches use the ZOB immediately behind (east of) Bremen Hauptbahnhof, a couple of minutes from the platforms. FlixBus dominates and tickets are cheapest booked online in advance; machines and a small service point are at the terminal rather than a full ticket office. Hamburg takes about 1h30 by coach, Berlin roughly 5h and Amsterdam around 5h30, with most other European journeys routed through Hamburg or Hanover.

ferry.note: Bremen lies about 60 km up the Weser from the North Sea, so there are no international ferries here; the deep-sea, cruise and Ro-Ro terminals are down at Bremerhaven, an hour away by regional train. Hal over runs harbour and Weser cruises from the Schlachte promenade in the centre, plus all-day excursions downriver to Bremerhaven and a small passenger ferry to Lankenauer Hoft that runs weekends from April to October. For a Baltic or North Sea crossing you would travel to Hamburg, Kiel or Lubeck-Travemunde.

half.name: Hamburg

half.name: Worpswede
